parts.title: Shared mathematical foundations
parts.summary: Start with dimensions, inner products, isometries and explicit conventions. The same foundations support state preparation, block encoding and later quantum-information arguments.

parts.title: State Preparation
parts.summary: Reason from a target amplitude family to normalization, structural representations and a preparation construction. Inspect sparse and zero boundaries before transferring an argument to a circuit interface.

parts.title: Block Encoding and oracle composition
parts.summary: Track the represented operator, its normalizer and the accepted subspace. Keep preparation, SELECT, unprepare, workspace cleanup and resource tiers visible when composing constructions.

parts.title: Quantum Information
parts.summary: Study state and channel representations, symmetry and tensor structure through primary-source-grounded problems. Planned curriculum anchors are not local Lean closure for the complete answers.

parts.title: Quantum Scientific Computing
parts.summary: Follow the roles of input states, operator access, polynomial transformations and output interpretation. Source-only algorithm questions keep their assumptions and query/gate/readout boundaries explicit.
